audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (first fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_a_paeds.json, _a_obgyn.json, _a_psych.json and _a_medicine.json, one file per module. Split 12 Paediatrics, 12 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 13 Psychiatry and 13 Medicine; tier mix 24 L3, 22 L4 and 4 L5 with no L2 and no L1, taking the bank to 6492 with all four modules exactly level on 1623. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1611 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1610, with deficits measured against the full per-topic total including the legacy L1 and L2 questions, as Section 2 requires. L3 deficits were 13.94 points in Paediatrics, 13.50 in Obstetrics, 12.67 in Medicine and 11.68 in Psychiatry, and L4 deficits were 13.34, 12.85, 11.89 and 10.84 respectively, while L5 sat at 4.97 per cent in every module, that is marginally below its 5 per cent target, giving every L5 cell a small positive deficit of about 0.03 points. The strict per-question argmax remains degenerate for the ninth consecutive fire and this fire quantified it again: simulated unconstrained across all twelve cells it allocates 43 of 50 questions to Paediatrics and takes the module spread from 1 to 42, breaching the Section 2 requirement that all four modules stay within about 10. This fire therefore allocated 12/12/13/13, which brings all four modules to exactly 1623 and honours the tie-break clause pointing toward the lower-count modules, Psychiatry and Medicine. Within each module the tier split followed the ideal shape rather than the raw argmax, because L3 leads L4 by only 0.54 to 0.84 points in every module while that gap closes at roughly 0.06 points per question added, so a strict argmax would return an almost pure L3 batch and reopen the L4 deficit it had just closed. Departure from the previous fire, recorded deliberately: the 2026-09-15 fire generated zero L5 on the reading that L5 was at or fractionally above target. L5 has since drifted to 4.97 per cent, so its deficit is now positive and a batch of 50 with no L5 would have pushed it down to 4.94 per cent. This fire therefore generated one L5 per module, which holds L5 at 4.99 per cent in all four modules rather than letting the tier decay. The structural point the previous fire raised for the maintainer still stands: because L5 is close to its target its deficit can never exceed the 11 to 14 point deficits carried by L3 and L4, so a strict argmax reading will never select an L5 cell and the tier needs an explicit floor or per-batch quota if sustained L5 growth is wanted. Audit: valid JSON, zero em-dashes and zero non-ASCII characters, zero banned tokens, every question difficulty 3, 4 or 5, answer-length parity max to min at or under 1.35 on all 50, with the highest ratio 1.242, correct letters exactly 10 per letter A to E, source_refs all resolving to declared source labels, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, reference_ranges keys all valid, vitals in fixed order or compressed to within normal limits, data_table values all flat strings, no lead-in guideline leak, no pertinent-negative pile-up, no parenthetical qualifier in any correct option, no correct option uniquely carrying a numeral, no weight-based dose arithmetic in any lead-in, explanation.summary 3 to 5 sentences with 3 to 5 key points and a specific pearl on every question. Six defects across four categories were found on audit and fixed before publication: a draft artefact left inside an option rationale in the adjustment disorder item; three explanation summaries running to six sentences, in the post-stroke emotionalism, monoamine oxidase inhibitor perioperative and insulinoma items; a pertinent-negative pile-up of six closures in the Helicobacter pylori stem, rewritten to none by converting them to positive statements; and an alcohol related hepatitis item whose correct option was the only one carrying a numeral, corrected by adding numeric specificity to three distractors. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new was run against the 6442 pre-existing questions and FAILED on the first run, flagging one Medicine question at 0.764 combined and 0.85 answer similarity: a Barrett oesophagus surveillance-interval item duplicating med-0915f-03 published the previous day. The keyword pre-screen had missed it because the existing question describes the segment as columnar lined lower oesophagus and never uses the word Barrett, which is precisely the synonym-variant failure the gate exists to catch. That question was replaced outright with a primary biliary cholangitis item on inadequate biochemical response to ursodeoxycholic acid at twelve months, and the gate was re-run and passed with zero duplicates; intra-batch self comparison also returned zero pairs at or above 0.62. No threshold was altered and the script was not modified.
